utterances.text: Now, we know that the attack took place, and I would like to quote back to you what you said yesterday at page 29 of the proceedings. And you said, "These are blocking positions in Dutch as well, south of Srebrenica, and first of all, their purpose was to block the approaching Serbian troops and, 2, they were intended to create a situation so that if they tried to continue approaching Srebrenica, they would be in a situation where they had no choice but to attack the UN as well."

utterances.speaker: CORNELIS HENDRIK NICOLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: In other words, the Dutch Battalion were going to try and block the VRS attack by forcing the VRS to attack the Dutch. Is that right? Is that what you were saying?

utterances.speaker: CORNELIS HENDRIK NICOLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You could express it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Your men placed themselves strategically between the VRS and the Bosniak fighters. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: CORNELIS HENDRIK NICOLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They placed themselves between the VRS and the town of Srebrenica with the civilian population.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: All right. Let's have a look at the document on the screen. Next paragraph, if we've got it there, "The BiH will continue to try to block DutchBat in their OPs or in positions in front of the BiH. This will involve the use of force. They cannot" -- I beg your pardon, start again. "They can co-locate with UN positions to use them as human shields. This might provoke a reaction from the BSA with a risk for UN personnel to get caught in cross-fire between both factions. The BiH is likely to attempt to capture weapons and vehicles from DutchBat to compensate for their lack of armament." Now, that is what happened, isn't it? The VRS wanted to get at the Bosniak fighters. Your men stood in the middle, and the Bosniak fighters wanted to get near your men in order to encourage the VRS to attack them, UNPROFOR, rather than the Bosniak fighters. That's what happened.

utterances.speaker: CORNELIS HENDRIK NICOLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that point, the role of the UN was to keep the warring parties apart and that was done to the best of our ability, but I admit that we were only partially successful because from our observation posts, we could do very little about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: It's obvious, isn't it, that UNPROFOR, the UN, your Dutch soldiers, were not the target of the VRS? That's right, isn't it, General?

utterances.speaker: CORNELIS HENDRIK NICOLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I seriously contest that, because then otherwise I don't know why the observation posts were shot at.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Weren't there Bosniak trenches next to the DutchBat positions?

utterances.speaker: CORNELIS HENDRIK NICOLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not in the enclave personally so I don't know the exact location of Bosniak trenches. You would need to ask Colonel Karremans about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: And I suppose you can't help as to whether there was any fire from those trenches in the direction of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: CORNELIS HENDRIK NICOLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that BiH soldiers also shot at VRS positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Now, I'm suggesting to you that UNPROFOR was not the enemy of the VRS. What do you say about that?

utterances.speaker: CORNELIS HENDRIK NICOLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, perhaps that's officially the case, but nonetheless, the VRS did attack UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: And I suggest to you, as evidence of the fact that they didn't actually attack UNPROFOR but were in fact attacking the Bosniak fighters, not one of your men was killed, let alone injured, by the VRS in the attack that you have told us about. Correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer? One moment. Yes, Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, that's not consistent with the evidence that's been presented in this case. That is a misstatement of the evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This has been also discussed before. So -- and the question put and answered in a different form. So let him answer this question now and proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Can you answer the question, please, General?

utterances.speaker: CORNELIS HENDRIK NICOLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't object to answering. I merely attribute it to our good luck that there were no casualties among the Dutch soldiers at that moment, but it is a fact that both OPs and APCs of DutchBat were shot at by the VRS, and I would call that a hostile act.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: And I'm really are not being flippant here but it is simply a strange quirk of fate, is it, that the unfortunate Dutch soldier who was killed happened to be killed by Bosniak fire?

utterances.speaker: CORNELIS HENDRIK NICOLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now, what is your question in this?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Well, I'm asking you whether it's a coincidence, a strange quirk of fate? As I say, it's not a flippant question.

utterances.speaker: CORNELIS HENDRIK NICOLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that could certainly be called bizarre.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I'd like to go back, if I may, to where I began, and that is examining briefly P2906, Lieutenant-Colonel De Ruiter's note of your conversation with my client, and to assist, because there were some e-court problems yesterday, we now have hard copies of P2374 which was the Muslim intercept. Now, I asked you a fair amount about this yesterday and I'm not going to go over it again but at page 76, in the course of my cross-examination yesterday evening, I invited you to give examples in this document of the nonsense and lies that you allege General Gvero was uttering, and you said this: "All allegations that UN soldiers were not being attacked or rather that it was not" and now here come the important words, "They were not being attacked by the VRS but by Muslims, that's nonsense and lies, truly." Now, what is beyond doubt is that your men came under attack by the Muslims. That was not a lie, was it?

utterances.speaker: CORNELIS HENDRIK NICOLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were attacked by the VRS, and in addition, what also happened was that the BiH soldiers tried to impede the withdrawal of the UN soldiers and in that course of events, there was also shooting at DutchBat. That's what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Would you agree that Dutch Battalion were attacked by the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: CORNELIS HENDRIK NICOLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I wouldn't see it that way. As long as DutchBats remained in their OPs and performed their duties, they were not attacked by the Muslim troops, only when they wanted to leave their positions were -- did they encounter an impediment on the part of the BiH.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Now, as far as you are concerned, the VRS treated UNPROFOR as an enemy and attacked them. That's what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: CORNELIS HENDRIK NICOLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I need to establish a distinction there, to the extent that they attacked the observation posts and shot at the compound, there was an attack by the VRS. On the other hand, I have to say that the UN soldiers that surrendered at their observation posts, they were treated well by the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Could we have a look at P33, please? Now, this, General Nicolai, is a document from Major General Tolimir to the president of the Republika Srpska for information, the Drina Corps forward command post and to Generals Gvero and Krstic personally. And could we scroll down to the bottom? It's conduct of combat operations around Srebrenica. And it says: "In accordance with the order of the president of the Republika Srpska, you must issue an order to all combat units participating in combat operations around Srebrenica to offer maximum protection and safety to all UNPROFOR members and the civilian Muslim population. You must order subordinate units to refrain from destroying civilian targets unless forced to do so because of strong enemy resistance. Ban the torching of residential buildings and treat the civilian population and war prisoners in accordance with the Geneva Conventions of 12 August 1949." And it's dated, this particular document, the 9th of July of 1995. Have you seen this before?

utterances.speaker: CORNELIS HENDRIK NICOLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: You weren't aware, therefore, I assume, that Tolimir had sent out this direction?

utterances.speaker: CORNELIS HENDRIK NICOLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Definitely not. The actions of the VRS at that point definitely did not correspond with what is being propagated here.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: You do agree, though, don't you, that the purpose of the VRS attack was not directed against UNPROFOR? The purpose, the motive, behind it had nothing to do with UNPROFOR, did it?

utterances.speaker: CORNELIS HENDRIK NICOLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The presumed underlying reason for the attack was, as it was expected, that the VRS wanted to diminish the size of the enclave and to achieve this, the observation posts had to be attacked so any way you look at it, the fact remains that the UN military was attacked by the VRS, whatever the reason may have been.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: And you gained the distinct impression in your conversation of the 11th of July with Gvero that he was lying when he said that the VRS was not attacking UNPROFOR positions?

utterances.speaker: CORNELIS HENDRIK NICOLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Would you be surprised if you had been receiving reports that the UN is being attacked for four consecutive days and they still keep insisting that that's not the case, then of course, you can understand that I was highly sceptical about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: That may be, but as we can see in the document from General Janvier, certainly Zagreb had anticipated exactly this happening and your battalion, being caught in the cross fire between the warring parties but not actually being the target of the warring parties. You must have realised that, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: CORNELIS HENDRIK NICOLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: But that won't change the fact that there is no justification for attacking UN troops. Just because you expect it, that doesn't make it justified.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Now, we are clearly not going to agree on this, but I'd like to show you -- I think you're acknowledging what I've just said. I'd like to show you what General Gvero did immediately after this conversation. Could we have 6D207 in e-court, please? We'll remember as we look at this document that your conversation with my client was at 1615 hours on the 11th of July and here we have a document, we've got the original there, get the translation in a moment, also dated the 11th of July 1995, and handwritten in the right-hand corner is it was received, wherever this was recovered from, at 1735 on that day, so under an hour and a half after your conversation. It's headed top secret. It's a warning on treatment of UNPROFOR personnel in the enclave of Srebrenica. "In relation to the total situation in the enclave of Srebrenica, the monitoring of reactions from UNPROFOR representatives and the world public opinion indicates that the attitude of the army of the Republika Srpska personnel towards UNPROFOR personnel and units in the area of Srebrenica is in the focus of attention. To that end, Drina Corps command, acting through its subordinate commands, will ensure utmost decency in the attitude towards UNPROFOR personnel, our guests, and prevent any actions and provocation directing against UNPROFOR units in the enclave regardless of their behaviour. Such attitude towards UNPROFOR units is at this moment of multifarious importance for the realisation of the assignment at hand and of our set objectives." And it's signed assistant commander Major-General Milan Gvero. This document suggests and supports my proposition that Gvero was not lying when he said that the VRS was not attacking UNPROFOR positions. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: CORNELIS HENDRIK NICOLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I certainly don't agree with that. There was shooting at UNPROFOR positions for four consecutive days in a row, so whatever is stated on paper, the facts were clearly different.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: And this document is also suggestive, is it not -- rephrase that. This document doesn't in any way suggest or support your proposition that this man threatened you just an hour earlier. Here he is telling his men to treat UNPROFOR with the utmost respect, isn't he?

utterances.speaker: CORNELIS HENDRIK NICOLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I repeat that the facts were different, and if General Gvero in his conversation with me tells me that I will be responsible for what happens to the civilian population, then there must have been some threat somewhere to the civilian population because why else would he say that?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Well, we went over that yesterday and I'm not going to go over it again now. But what's clear from this document is he's heeded what you said and he's tried to do something about it, hasn't he?

utterances.speaker: CORNELIS HENDRIK NICOLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's possible that he wrote this down and intended to do something about it but up to that point, as UNPROFOR, we noticed nothing of all that. So please excuse me if I had an entirely different impression of the situation at that moment than is indicated by this statement in writing.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: And your impression had been obtained, excuse me, your impression of the situation had been obtained, hadn't it, from all the various sources of confused information that you were receiving, and your general view that anyone in the VRS must be bad and must be anti-UNPROFOR? That's where you were coming from, General Nicolai.

utterances.speaker: CORNELIS HENDRIK NICOLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, your remark comes across as being highly suggestive to me, and I vehemently protest. My information at that time was not confused at all. Previously, we spoke about confused information in the days after the enclave had fallen, up to the point that the enclave fell the information was not confused at all, and I continuously received accurate reports from DutchBat and was particularly well informed about what was happening. As for prejudices regarding any party at all, I take distance from that because that was not the case at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I'm not really concerned about whether you are or are not prejudiced against the VRS. What I'm suggesting to you, sir, is that you've tarred my client with the same brush that you tarred others who perhaps deserve it and you simply are not being objective about the matters to which you've attested.

utterances.speaker: CORNELIS HENDRIK NICOLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I contest that as well. What I care about is not your client in person. What I care about is that on 11 July a threat was expressed regarding the civilian population that was in and around the compound, and all I tried to do was to avert the possibility of a blood bath there.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: And that's exactly why you have tarred him with the same brush. That threat may well have been uttered. You came can into this Court. You attributed it to him. I've shown you documents and the result is surely you concede you didn't come in here with a fair and open mind in relation to General Gvero?

utterances.speaker: CORNELIS HENDRIK NICOLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can repeat what I said previously but there would be no added value to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Could Your Honour give us a few moments? I know that General Gvero would like to speak to Mr. Krgovic in court initially and perhaps I'll revert to Chamber if in a moment, if I may.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please speak a bit away from the microphone? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Too late in the day, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I've just been asked to ask you this, and I know we went over it yesterday and if need be, I can show you the documentation again. Indeed you've got the actual intercept in front of you there in hard copy. But you did concede yesterday that on the face of the intercept there was certainly no threat to shell the compound in Potocari. There is no question about that, is there?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think this was asked and answered already.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Well, that's right, Your Honour. I'm getting some instructions in relation to this matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Go ahead. Go ahead. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I don't want to revisit our battle of yesterday, General, but I've been asked to ask you that question. Do you agree with what I've just said?

utterances.speaker: CORNELIS HENDRIK NICOLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can go back to what was said yesterday. We observed from the transcripts that General Gvero did not say literally in that phone conversation that he would shoot at the compound and its surroundings. He did refer to the danger to the civilian population or consequences for the civilian population, and that combined with a threat that we had learned of that the civilian population would be shot at if we did not discontinue the air attacks led us to discontinue the air attacks. I admit, though, from -- it's not clear that General Gvero said this in so many words from the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. That's enough, I think. We've heard enough on this now.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Again, could I just have one moment? The Chamber will be relieved to know that I've finished this cross-examination, and I'm grateful to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Sarapa, you had --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- not confirmed yesterday definitely that you have no cross-examination. You don't have a cross-examination, I take it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Only one question. I said that I might have or might need ten minutes at the most, but I'll have just one question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. General. My name is Djordje Sarapa and I'm here defending General Pandurevic. I will only have one question for you, as you heard. In your statement you gave to the Tribunal dated the 18th of November, the following: [In English] I have informed the Dutch Minister of Defence of the planned evacuation [Realtime transcript read in error "vehicles"] and our intention to use UNPROFOR tracks and he had agreed to this." [Interpretation] Do you still stand by that statement of yours?

utterances.speaker: CORNELIS HENDRIK NICOLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only spoke with the minister about our intention to evacuate the civilian population. I did not discuss with him how we would be doing that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: I apologise. The transcript doesn't reflect the statement clearly. This is 6D153, page 13. It wasn't recorded correctly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You read it in English, no?

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It says here, the planned vehicles. In the English text that I read, it says, I have informed the Dutch Minister of Defence of the planned evacuation and our intention to use UNPROFOR tracks, and he had agreed to this."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The minister said he agreed with the intention to evacuate the civilian population and that UNPROFOR would assist with that. But at the point when I was speaking with the Minister of Defence, even I didn't know what means we would use to that end.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Sarapa. Mr. Thayer, do you have a re-examination?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Borovcanin? Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I don't wish to cross-examine the witness, just to assist Mr. Sarapa. On two occasions he referred to the date 11th of July, and it's not in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I see. Okay. But does that change your answer, General? When Mr. Sarapa put the question to you, he was obviously referring to the 11th of July. That went missing in the transcript. What I would like to know from you is whether you would have answered differently.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think so. The conversation with Defence took place at around 5.00 or half past 5.00 in the afternoon of the 11th and all we discussed was the intention to evacuate and the assistance of UNPROFOR with that evacuation because that's an important decision. The minister agreed with that and I personally had no idea about how we would take it from there. That's the answer that I have to give to this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. And thank you, Mr. Lazarevic. Mr. Thayer, do you have a re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I do, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. How long is it going to last?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I don't think I can complete it before the -- if we break at 12.30, I don't think I'll be able to complete it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I would say 20 minutes, maybe half an hour. I will keep it as tight and quick as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, General.

utterances.speaker: CORNELIS HENDRIK NICOLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: You testified that you were in contact during the attack with Colonel Franken among others, Colonel Karremans' deputy commander, do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: CORNELIS HENDRIK NICOLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It depended who answered the phone at that point, but I did speak with Major Franken on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you recall receiving any information from Major Franken that he had received information that DutchBat peacekeepers had been injured during the course of the VRS attacks on the OPs?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Josse?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Leading question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. You are right. Avoid leading questions because obviously you're going to face objections. And you know what the policy is.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall receiving any information from Major Franken regarding any injuries to DutchBat peacekeepers during the operation?

utterances.speaker: CORNELIS HENDRIK NICOLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Josse. One moment, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Again it's a leading question. The question should be did you receive any information from Major Franken; if so, what was it. Otherwise, it's leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You're 100 per cent right.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, it's a yes or no answer and he said no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah, but it was a leading question because you inserted the "injuries" aspect in it. The way it should have been put is as suggested or as indicated by Mr. Josse. Anyway, for the record, Mr. Josse, and Mr. Thayer, because the transcript must be faithful, must faithfully reflect, I did hear the witness distinctly answer no to the question and this is not reflected in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Well, I'm quite happy to have that in the transcript, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And you confirm that, don't you, General?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The only report I received about DutchBat who were wounded was the death of Private Ari Van Renssen.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, I want to turn your attention, General, to the reports you were receiving, particularly on the 6th and 7th of July. You were asked some questions regarding the level of activity on those two days and with respect to casualties that were taken in those two days. I want to show you some UNMO reports which we'll have to put on the ELMO. These have all been previously disclosed to Defence counsel. We will be applying for 65 ter numbers for all of the UNMO reports. These are in connection with Colonel Kingori's upcoming testimony, witness, for whom the Trial Chamber granted permission to add to our 65 ter list of witnesses. For the record, I will be showing General Nicolai 00527524 to 7526. Do you have the document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: CORNELIS HENDRIK NICOLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And we can see the date of this is July 6th, covering the period from one minute after midnight to 2000 hours on July 6; is that correct, General?

utterances.speaker: CORNELIS HENDRIK NICOLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Actually I've been informed that we do have a 65 ter number for this and it's 490.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And we will be looking at the bottom of this page. Do you see the section, general, where it says, "Team Srebrenica reported a BSA offensive launched and ongoing within the enclave as reported under separate cover? The BSA used tanks, artillery, mortars, rockets and heavy machine-gun and have targeted the DutchBat headquarters, Bandera Triangle, DutchBat OPs U and S," and then it looks like, is that south, that abbreviation there, STH?

utterances.speaker: CORNELIS HENDRIK NICOLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, south.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: "Of OP hotel. Potocari township, Srebrenica township, at least 250 artillery and mortar rounds have been recorded so far. The UNMO team have confirmed two fatalities and six casualties so far being taken to hospital. DutchBat reported 620-millimetre rockets landed close to their compound with only two exploding at about 0330 hours on July 6. The shelling of the surrounding area, however, continued until about 1600 hours on the 6th," and if we go to the next page, "with two civilian casualties so far recorded. We move a little further, "at 1450 hours, the OP came under direct shelling from company held by the BSA." General, how does this information square with the information you were receiving from, among others, the DutchBat command?

utterances.speaker: CORNELIS HENDRIK NICOLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It corresponds perfectly with the reports that DutchBat issued.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I want to show you another UNMO report. We are done with that, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Josse?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Well, I would submit that at the very minimum, the witness should be asked whether he'd previously seen this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Any way --

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: If the Court is not with me, I'm not pressing the point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's -- because this is something that is reserved to the person doing the examination, in this case, the re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He may decide it's not a pertinent question and we are not going to intervene, anyway, but if you think it's a pertinent thing to find out, you put the question. If not, let's go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm just going to move along and try to conclude this as quickly as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I'm showing you what has been marked as 00527527 to 7532. That's 65 ter 491.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Wait, General. Yes, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I'm going to develop my argument and objection this way. If my learned friend chooses to do it in this manner, then in my submission, this is really another form of leading. I would have personally no objection if he first asked the witness what recollection he has based on the information he'd received and then showed him the document. But realistically, this is leading in a veiled form otherwise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, my friend put this witness's recollection in question, challenged his recollection about when certain things occurred, whether there were casualties, what day certain activities occurred, indeed, whether on a certain day there was heightened activity or any activity at all. I think it's perfectly appropriate to show him these documents in this manner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Then do introduce each document properly to the witness and I suppose I go back on what I stated earlier, I think it would be more appropriate if you asked the witness whether he's familiar with this document and whether he was familiar with this document at the relevant time and then you proceed from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, do you have the document in front of you, again this is 65 ter 491. And I'd ask to you look at the first page. Can you tell the Court what this is?

utterances.speaker: CORNELIS HENDRIK NICOLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a daily situation report from the Sector North-East, from Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And in the course of your duties, would this type of information pass through you or your staff?

utterances.speaker: CORNELIS HENDRIK NICOLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The staff received reports such as these every day, and based on that, the briefings were prepared for the commander and the other staff members.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And would the information contained in these reports be passed on to you if your staff deemed it important enough?

utterances.speaker: CORNELIS HENDRIK NICOLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Such a report could be cause to discuss a certain situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Leading question. That's the objection to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It needs a lot of thinking, Mr. Josse. We are going to have a break now. No, not really. I think we can proceed, actually, but we'll have the break now.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Well, I certainly could do with a cup of coffee, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: General, would you just describe please how information in this type of sit-rep would reach your ears?

utterances.speaker: CORNELIS HENDRIK NICOLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As part of the task of the Chief of Staff on the basis of the reports from the various sectors, an overall assessment would be made for the whole area of Bosnia-Herzegovina, since as the Chief of Staff I was co-responsible for these reports, it was my task to check whether the overall reports were in line with what was reported from the sectors. So I would read these reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Let's look at page 2 of this report, please. We will be looking at paragraph 1. The section that reads, "Potocari compound was targeted several times during the day, OP Foxtrot was hit by several tank rounds which caused great damage to the watch tower. No UN casualties reported. In Srebrenica enclave, an artillery impact killed a civilian and injured a boy." Sir, do you recall receiving any information concerning OP Foxtrot being hit by several tank rounds resulting in the damage described here? Do you recall receiving any information specifically?

utterances.speaker: CORNELIS HENDRIK NICOLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I received that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you recall with any specificity receiving any reports about an artillery impact killing a civilian and injuring a boy? I know it's 12 years ago, but do you have any specific recollection of receiving that information?

utterances.speaker: CORNELIS HENDRIK NICOLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not the details of that information, but I read all those sit-reps so I undoubtedly saw it at the time. Of course, I can't remember the details of each and every daily sit-rep.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. I'd like to go to the next document, the ERN is 00527533 to 7535. So we are done with the previous report. And this is 65 ter number 492, please. And I do have hard copies if it's easier for you to read, General.

utterances.speaker: CORNELIS HENDRIK NICOLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That would be convenient. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recognise what type of document this is, sir?

utterances.speaker: CORNELIS HENDRIK NICOLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: One moment, please. I'd like to have a look at what this is.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Please take your time, General.

utterances.speaker: CORNELIS HENDRIK NICOLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. I've seen it. This is a daily sit-rep of the UNMOs from the Sector North-East headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And would you just take a moment, please, and describe for the Trial Chamber the UNMOs chain of command and how it fit into the UNPROFOR chain of command, in terms of reporting, I think, would be the most salient?

utterances.speaker: CORNELIS HENDRIK NICOLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The UNMOs reported to every level within UNPROFOR. There were -- no, there were UNMOs within every level of UNPROFOR. And the UNPROFORs from the sectors reported to the UNMO chief in Sarajevo, and the UNMO chief in Sarajevo in turn reported to the chief UNMO in Zagreb. And that's how all information was gathered, and on that basis, the situation was assessed.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And how would UNMO information be reported to you, General?

utterances.speaker: CORNELIS HENDRIK NICOLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That information, the UNMO reports, went to the operations section, which used it as complementary information to the reports that came from the unit commanders. So it complemented the reports from the units.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, the document we are looking at is dated 7 July. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: CORNELIS HENDRIK NICOLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what is the time range covered by this particular report, if you could just share that with us?

utterances.speaker: CORNELIS HENDRIK NICOLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It involves the day July the 7th, from midnight until 8.00 in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: You were asked some questions by my friend about what was or wasn't going on on the 7th of July, in terms of the VRS attack. I want to ask you some specific questions about this report which covers that period of time. Do you see under paragraph 3, military information, "DutchBat reported heavy shelling around their compound in Potocari and as a result three men were injured and brought by MSF to the hospital." Do you see that, General?

utterances.speaker: CORNELIS HENDRIK NICOLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: UNMOs confirm this. Reports of more shelling at 1500 hours. "Three shells landed in Srebrenica and injured two men. One was picked up by our patrol and the other one by MSF but he died on arrival at the hospital." Further on, "A lot of damage on buildings has been caused in that area, despite the low casualty figure." Sir, do you recall receiving this level of information on the 7th, given -- well, I'll just leave it at that.

utterances.speaker: CORNELIS HENDRIK NICOLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. We received these reports on a daily basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I want to turn your attention to the second page and just follow up with one last question about this day. Under paragraph C, summary of meetings --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, one moment. Yes, Mr. Josse?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Bearing in mind how Mr. Thayer has explained this line of re-examination, at page 64, line 12 onwards, isn't he in effect cross-examining his own witness? Because of course, I simply put the witness's statement to him, and in effect he's trying to impeach his own witness. If he's saying that this man lacks credibility in accordance with the Trial Chamber's previous ruling, then of course he's allowed to do that but he needs to declare that openly and then proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you wish to comment on that, Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't think I need to make any comment about this witness's credibility. I think this witness's recollection was placed in direct issue and I'm entitled to follow up and see if this affects his recollection one way or the other. That was going to be my final question after reviewing this second page of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Could I just say that's exactly the point? In relation to this rather narrow issue, as to the 7th of July, this particular line of re-examination must amount to a cross-examination as to credit. My learned friend needs to make a decision. Either he declares him -- declares that he's going to impeach him under the Trial Chamber's guidelines or he's not permitted to do this. He can't have it both ways.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's a majority decision. Basically we don't think that Mr. Thayer is in any way cross-examining the witness or trying to impeach the -- his own witness. The opinion of the majority is that Mr. Thayer is trying to jog the memory of the witness and see if he can recollect further details that might explain better his previous testimony. So go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. If we may scroll all the way down in the English, please, I just want to catch the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, because I have to --

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: There we go. Thank you. And we'll have to turn the next page on the B/C/S to capture that as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Under the UNMO team comment heading, General, at the -- about -- with about a third of the paragraph left to go, you'll see it says UNMO team comment. Do you see that portion? This is towards the bottom of paragraph C 1.

utterances.speaker: CORNELIS HENDRIK NICOLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: "The BSA offensive seems to be steadily intensifying, whatever their aims are, they seem to be concentrating more on civilian targets in Srebrenica town and Potocari. There are several civilian casualties and unassessed damage to civilian property." My question, General, is simple: You testified that to your recollection, July 7th was I think a relatively calm day or peaceful day or something to that effect and that to that extent the warning that described shelling on the 7th was incorrect. I just want to find out whether, having seen these portions, whether that changes your recollection at all or whether it's the same.

utterances.speaker: CORNELIS HENDRIK NICOLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stick to the main outline of my statement. All is relative. No day passed without incidents. But in comparison to what happened on the 6th, or the 8th, the 7th, by comparison, was a more quiet day.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. General. One last report to show you. This is ERN 00527573 to 7577 and that is 65 ter number 506. And we'll start by looking at page 2 of this document. And I'm being informed by Ms. Stewart that actually this document has been split so that second page is 507. My apologies. And again I have hard copies if that's more convenient for you, General.

utterances.speaker: CORNELIS HENDRIK NICOLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: General, what's the date and time on this UNMO report?

utterances.speaker: CORNELIS HENDRIK NICOLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: July the 11th, 1415 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. I think you need to flip the page. Do you see some numbers? There you go. There is 00527574 should be the number at the top of your page. This was the document that got split up so... What is the date and time of this UNMO report, General?

utterances.speaker: CORNELIS HENDRIK NICOLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: July the 11th, 1620 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: General, this report reads, "At this moment, the stream of refugees and wounded is incountable any more. We figure that a total of 20.000 refugees came to the DutchBat compound of Potocari already and is growing steadily. Since our last report the shelling of the town has been going on despite of the air strikes. The town is in the hands of the BSA by now and the latest ultimatum given by the BSA is that if the air strikes continue, everything inside the enclave will be bombed. Also, UNPROFOR and the other UN organisations." Now, I think we can all agree that your first conversation with General Gvero was on the 11th of July at either 1615 or 1610, depending on whether we are looking at Colonel De Ruiter's notes or the actual Muslim intercept. There is a difference of five minutes. My question is does this help you at all in terms of recalling at what point you received information about the stream of refugees arriving into the Potocari compound?

utterances.speaker: CORNELIS HENDRIK NICOLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This report in any case confirms information that I had already received orally previously.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you have any recollection of receiving this information about the latest ultimatum as being tied to an UNMO report?

utterances.speaker: CORNELIS HENDRIK NICOLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said yesterday that I didn't exactly recall how reports reached me, but this report makes it highly likely that this was communicated to our headquarters both in writing and orally.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay, General. We are done with that document. Just a few more questions. When you were interviewed by the investigator from the Office of the Prosecutor in the fall of 1996, do you recall exactly what you told him about your conversation with General Gvero at 1615 hours on 11 July?

utterances.speaker: CORNELIS HENDRIK NICOLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would have to check my witness statement on that. I don't recall whether we dwelled on that conversation at length.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, let's do that, then. It's 6D153 and we are going to look at page 13 of the English and that begins on page 12 of the B/C/S and continues very quickly on to page 13 of the B/C/S. And it's at the very top of the page in English, General. "At 1615 hours on the 11 July I spoke with General Gvero at the VRS HQ. During that call I explained why we were using air power. General Gvero was denying that they were attacking UNPROFOR positions and was demanding that we should stop the air attacks immediately. I answered by saying that we would only stop the attacks when they stopped attacking the enclave and had withdrawn. He said that he could and did not have to stop anything, as neither UNPROFOR nor the civilian population was being attacked. He threatened me by saying that I would be held responsible for all further developments, the destiny of my men and the civilian population in Srebrenica." General, did you say that to the investigator in 1996?

utterances.speaker: CORNELIS HENDRIK NICOLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Clearly, I did. I also signed this statement for my approval.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you stand by that statement, General?

utterances.speaker: CORNELIS HENDRIK NICOLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I do, and it is in line with what I've attested so far here.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, I just want to show you -- or ask you one more series of questions, General. Do you remember being debriefed by Dutch authorities in Assen in September of 1995? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: CORNELIS HENDRIK NICOLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you recall what, if anything, you told the authorities who were interviewing you at that time about this conversation that you had with General Gvero?

utterances.speaker: CORNELIS HENDRIK NICOLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In that case, too, I would have to have a look at that statement because I don't recall off the top of my head what I said at various points in time in various statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, I have it in both English and Dutch in hard copy. Would you prefer to have it in English or in Dutch, General?

utterances.speaker: CORNELIS HENDRIK NICOLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I don't think this is in e-court. I can put a hard copy on the ELMO very quickly, and this will be my last couple of questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: We think it probably is in e-court, if it assists.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: That will be helpful, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: What date is this again, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: This is the statement on the 18th of September 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: We think it's 6D157.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And we will be looking at page 3 of the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Yes, we think it is there.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Again, we are talking about page 3 of the English and it would be page 4 of the Dutch. Do you see the portion, General, where it begins, "Immediately after the aircraft's departure"? It's about halfway through the document. You'll see there is a reference to a few times, 1100, 12, 15?

utterances.speaker: CORNELIS HENDRIK NICOLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you see where it says, "In the meantime, the battle on the ground continued as usual and B Company had to abandon its positions. The stream of refugees triggered by this action combined with the threats made by General Gvero in Pale to General Nicolai about bombing the stream of refugees, the Potocari compound and the immediate vicinity made it an urgent priority to stop any further deployment of the air force." General, did you say this to the authorities in Assen?

utterances.speaker: CORNELIS HENDRIK NICOLAI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, undoubtedly.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you stand by that statement, General?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You are going now -- there comes a point when I don't think we need your objection. I think you stop where you finished your last question and when you had your answer but not beyond that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. General, thank you, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. General Nicolai, we don't have any further questions for you, which means that your testimony ends here. We thank you very much for having been patient with us and for having come over to give testimony. And if you have to travel --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- travel safely.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Documents? Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I can recite the documents we would tender. With the exception of a few on redirect, they all appear on our original list of exhibits. They are 2750, 2751, 2753, 2906, 2907, 2909, 2972, 2973, 2974, 2975, 2976, 2978, P00490, P00491. Those are now the UNMO reports that we showed the witness on redirect. P00492. P00507. And that's it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Well, I'd like 30 seconds to digest those that were used in chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You can have one minute, Mr. Josse.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In the meantime, those who need no seconds to digest this list, do you have any objections? None.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, Mr. President, the Prosecution has no objections to the exhibits on the lists tendered by our friends.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Those that were used in the examination-in-chief, we have no objection to. So far as the two or was it four that were used in the re-examination, we would ask the Trial Chamber to give us until next week simply to reed those documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Fair enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I appreciate they've all got 65 ter numbers but I can't say we know all the documents off-hand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. You'll come back to us on Monday on these four documents, then, 490, 491, 492, 507.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. You have a list of documents, 6D204, 6D207. There is no objection from the Prosecution. Is there any objection from the other Defence teams? None. They are admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Obliged.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And there is 5D525 for the Miletic team. There is no objection, I take it. It is so admitted. Yes, Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, just to let the Court know, the one Exhibit 6D207 which has been accepted by the Court, came to us from the Defence team in the Krstic case, in case the Court has any questions about its provenance. It's our understanding that they got it from the RS government. We just wanted to let the Court know that's a subject of discussion and agreement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. McCloskey was good enough to discuss that with me during the last break and I'm grateful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. That concludes the Nicolai chapter. What's next? Are you in a position to bring forward Blaszczyk and do something concrete or should we adjourn?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I would say at this point better off just to adjourn trying to get him into the questions for the witness, I don't see ten minutes is worth it, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Yes, we will reconvene Monday morning and then we have an afternoon week next week. So be prepared to get tired. Have a nice weekend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 3rd day of December, 2007, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.33 p.m.,
